title: Action principles, restoration of BRS symmetry and the renormalization group equation for chiral non-Abelian gauge theories in dimensional renormalization with a non-anticommuting gamma5
journal: Nucl. Phys. B 572 (2000) 387 (journal ref not shown in the text accessed)
claim: One-loop renormalization of a general chiral non-Abelian gauge theory (left- and right-handed fermion multiplets, no scalars) in BMHV: the evanescent part of the fermion kinetic term breaks BRS invariance (s_d S_0 = Deltahat, eq. 34); the breaking is computed via the regularized action principles QAP1-QAP4 (eqs. 14-17) and Bonneau identities (eq. 25); the BRS anomaly is obtained for the first time in this framework (essential chiral anomaly, Sec. 3.6) and finite counterterms S_fct^(1) (ansatz eq. 66: (dA)^2, A box A, cubic and quartic gauge terms with d^{abc} and T^{abcd}, fermion kinetic and source terms) restore the ST identity iff d_{L-R}^{abc} = 0; the RGE is worked out in the anomaly-free case.
loop_order: 1 loop (explicit); all-order consistency of BMHV quoted from S3.02
theory: chiral non-Abelian gauge theory, simple and then general compact group, no scalars
scheme: BMHV DREG, MS for singular parts, finite counterterms fixed algebraically.
symmetry_argument: Regularized QAP: breaking = N[O].Gamma_ren (eq. 18); its finite four-dimensional part from Bonneau identities (residues of simple poles); cohomological split into removable (b-exact) part and anomaly.

proved: At one loop: BRS restorable by finite counterterms iff the gauge anomaly coefficient vanishes; explicit anomaly expression S(Gamma_ren) = (hbar/(4 pi)^2)(2/3) int eps Tr_{L-R}[omega d(dA A - (i/2) A A A)] + O(hbar^2).
assumed: Absence of anomaly at higher orders argued from the Adler-Bardeen theorem (expectation, not computed).

evidence: eqs. (11)-(18), (22)-(25): action principles and Bonneau identities.
eqs. (64), (66)-(67), Sec. 3.6: breaking, counterterm ansatz, anomaly.
eq. (39) discussion: multiplicative renormalization lost at one loop; eq. (40) stated valid to all orders.
red_flags: S3.08 (footnote 11 and footnote 17) reports disagreements with some ghost/group-factor terms of this paper (eq. 54).
Finite counterterms not unique (symmetric finite terms can be added).
